You can get [Irisalis Petals] through the following methods.
(Once the [Tracing the Trail] event ends, this method can no longer be used to get [Irisalis Petals].)

1. Main Story
Obtain them by clearing the following main story chapters: Ceremony Preparations, The Ceremony That Never Began, Colorful Fragrance, The Land of Dancing Illusions, The Land Where Dreams Come True, Ancient Sacred Fragrance, Rainbow of the Ground, and A New Journey.

2. Journey Quests
Obtain them by clearing the following Journey Quests: The Legend of Mist and Light, The Legend of Echoback Landing, The Legend of Flowers and Thorns, The Legend of the Land of Falling Stars, The Legend of Thousand-Fang Ridge, The Legend of the Land of Lightning and Thunder, The Legend of Helmuts and Helgons, The Legend of the Bell of Freedom, The Legend of the Berylline Vale, and The Legend of Driftwise Meadow.

3. Open-World Gathering
Gather them by following in Irelia’s footsteps across Breezy Plains.

4. First Alpha Clear
Obtain them by defeating a regional Alpha in Breezy Plains for the first time.

5. Elite Pathfinder Challenges
Obtain them by defeating the following elite Pathfinders in Breezy Plains or Astra: Wally, Jilly, Loulla, Aster, Wendell, Cecelia, and Lita.

6. Branch Nurturing
Obtain them by infusing energy into the Breezy Plains Branch and claiming its growth-stage rewards.

7. Breezy Plains Silver Badges
Obtain them by claiming Silver Badges from each area in Breezy Plains.

8. Aniimo Research
Unlock each family’s Nova Stage Aniimo Index entry, complete the research topic "Collect a Prismana Form Aniimo," and claim the corresponding reward.

9. Tracing the Trail
Obtain them by participating in the limited-time event [Tracing the Trail]. Once the event ends, this method can no longer be used to obtain [Irisalis Petals].

Graymane was one of the most legendary Flameruffs in his clan. He carried an intoxicating scent of flame, a trace left by countless battles, as if every strand of his fur burned with fighting spirit.
On the day his daughter was born, Graymane stood at the entrance to their den and looked toward Thousand-Fang Ridge in the distance. He made a vow: "Someday, I will make that tree bloom for me. When that day comes, my daughter will know her father is the strongest Scorchhowl."
But Graymane had one fatal flaw. He got lost very, very easily.
Whenever he set out to challenge a powerful foe, only one-twentieth of his time was spent fighting. The rest was spent finding his way. He once took a three-month detour to challenge a Glynsera in the north, only to stumble into a Bonesky family’s territory and send them scattering in fright. He also once chased prey all the way to the edge of Bloomville, where perfumers mistook him for a rare source of fragrance and chased him for three days and nights.
But Graymane never saw it as a problem. "Getting lost is training, too," he always told his daughter. "Every time I lose my way, I meet unexpected opponents and learn unexpected things."
His daughter grew older and slowly got used to her father coming home late. She no longer worried about whether he had been wounded in battle. She worried about whether he had gotten lost at the ends of the world again.
Then one day, Graymane told his daughter, "I am going to Thousand-Fang Ridge. I will earn the Ridgeback Tree’s recognition, just like Icho did. Once I make the Ridgeback Tree bloom for me, I will come home."
Graymane set out.
This time, he did not get lost. He found Thousand-Fang Ridge without a single wrong turn and stood before the withered Ridgeback Trees.
But he failed.
No matter how fiercely his fighting spirit burned, the dead trees gave no response. They stood in silence, as if quietly mocking his weakness.
"Maybe I am still not strong enough," Graymane told himself.
So he waited. He heard that Icho had appeared, and that Thousand-Fang Ridge had bloomed like flame. Graymane saw hope. If Icho could do it, surely he could, too.
He challenged Icho again and again, and lost again and again.
"As long as I become the strongest Scorchhowl, the Ridgeback Tree will recognize me." Graymane clung stubbornly to that belief.
But what he did not know was that the Ridgeback Tree had never bloomed for "the strongest."
Day after day, year after year, Graymane changed from a spirited wolf in his prime into an old wolf with gray-white fur. His fighting spirit wore away with each defeat, and his flame slowly died beneath the withered Ridgeback Tree.
Then one day, Graymane realized he could no longer leave Thousand-Fang Ridge. An invisible chain had appeared around his feet. It was a shackle he had placed on himself, forged from his obsession with "becoming the strongest" and his shame at going home to face his daughter.
He became an Inferlupa.
He no longer got lost, because he had nowhere left to go. Trapped in Thousand-Fang Ridge, he withered alongside the Ridgeback Trees. Sometimes he remembered his daughter, how she chased her own tail in circles when she was little, and the sparkle in her eyes when she asked, "Where did you get lost today, Dad?"
"Home... home..." Graymane the Inferlupa murmured. "Do I still have to keep fighting?"
What he did not know was that his daughter had never blamed him. That little Emberpup still waits outside the dead forest, believing her father is only a "lost fighter" who has not yet found his way home.
